title: Ex 3.3 #10 · P, R, O, F, S lists ending in S with O twice or more
prompt: Make lists of length 6 from the symbols P, R, O, F, S, with repetition allowed, such as (O, R, O, F, P, S). How many of these lists end in S and use the symbol O more than once?
answer_format: A whole number, or an expression for it like 26^4 or binom(10, 3).

mistakes.hint: That keeps every list with at least one O. 'More than once' means at least two O's, so the lists with exactly one O have to go too.
You removed the lists with exactly one O, but the lists with no O at all also fail.
Choosing two places for O and filling the rest freely counts a list with three or more O's several times.

hints: The last entry is fixed as S, so only the first five entries vary.
Among the first five entries, count the lists with no O and the lists with exactly one O, and subtract both from the total.
solution: The sixth entry must be S, so count the possibilities for the first five entries: $5^5 = 3125$ in all.
With no O, each of the five entries is P, R, F or S: $4^5 = 1024$ lists. With exactly one O, choose its position (5 ways) and fill the other four entries from P, R, F, S: $5 \cdot 4^4 = 1280$ lists.
So $3125 - 1024 - 1280 = 821$ lists end in S and use O more than once.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses the multiplication and subtraction principles (Sections 3.2 and 3.3).
